description: Dubu Jorim is a classic Korean side dish featuring pan-fried tofu simmered in a savory, spicy, and slightly sweet sauce. This comforting vegetarian dish offers a delightful texture contrast and bursts with authentic Korean flavors. It is perfect as a banchan or a main course served with a bowl of warm rice.

ingredients.notes: 14-16 oz, pressed to remove excess water

instructions.title: Prepare and Pan-Fry the Tofu
instructions.text: Press the tofu block for at least 30 minutes to remove excess water. Slice the pressed tofu into 1/2-inch thick rectangles. Heat 2 tablespoons of cooking oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Pan-fry the tofu slices until golden brown and slightly crispy on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove the tofu from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Braising Sauce
instructions.text: In a medium bowl, combine the soy sauce, gochugaru, minced garlic, sesame oil, sugar, and mirin if using. Whisk well until all ingredients are thoroughly mixed and the sugar has dissolved. This will be your flavorful braising sauce.

instructions.title: Assemble and Add Sauce to Pan
instructions.text: Arrange the pan-fried tofu slices neatly in a single layer in a wide, shallow pan or a large skillet. Pour the prepared braising sauce evenly over the tofu. Make sure each piece is coated.

instructions.title: Add Liquid and Simmer
instructions.text: Pour 1 cup of water or vegetable broth into the pan with the tofu and sauce. Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer over medium-high heat. Once simmering, reduce the heat to medium-low.

instructions.title: Braise the Tofu
instructions.text: Cover the pan and let the tofu braise in the sauce for about 15-20 minutes, or until most of the liquid has been absorbed and the sauce has thickened slightly. Periodically baste the tofu with the sauce to ensure even flavoring. The tofu should be tender and deeply flavored.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Once the Dubu Jorim is cooked, remove it from the heat. Garnish generously with sliced green onions and a sprinkle of sesame seeds. Serve immediately as a delicious banchan or main dish with freshly cooked rice. Enjoy the rich, spicy, and savory flavors.

tips: Always press your tofu thoroughly to remove excess water; this allows it to absorb the braising sauce more effectively and prevents it from crumbling.
For an extra layer of umami, you can add a pinch of dashima kelp powder to the braising sauce or use a mushroom-based broth instead of water.
Dubu Jorim tastes even better the next day as the flavors meld further. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.
article:
Discover the vibrant world of Korean vegetarian cuisine with a dish that tantalizes the taste buds and warms the soul: Dubu Jorim Spicy Braised Tofu. This beloved staple transforms humble tofu into an extraordinary culinary experience, marrying a firm texture with a rich, savory, and wonderfully spicy sauce. Perfect for a weeknight meal or a special occasion, this plant-based delight offers a hearty and satisfying option that's both healthy and incredibly flavorful. If you're looking to explore the depth of Korean flavors without meat, Dubu Jorim is an absolute must-try.

## What is Dubu Jorim Spicy Braised Tofu?

Dubu Jorim Spicy Braised Tofu is a classic Korean side dish (banchan) or main course, celebrated for its simplicity and robust flavors. "Dubu" means tofu, and "Jorim" refers to a cooking method where ingredients are simmered in a seasoned sauce until the liquid is significantly reduced and absorbed, resulting in a concentrated, flavorful glaze. In this dish, firm tofu slices are pan-fried until golden brown, then gently braised in a fiery gochugaru (Korean chili powder) and gochujang (Korean chili paste) based sauce, often enhanced with soy sauce, garlic, green onions, and a touch of sweetness.

What makes Dubu Jorim so special, particularly for those adhering to a vegetarian diet, is its ability to deliver a deeply savory and umami-rich experience typically associated with meat-based dishes. The tofu acts as a sponge, soaking up every nuance of the spicy, garlicky, and slightly sweet sauce. It's a testament to the ingenuity of Korean cooking, demonstrating how simple, plant-based ingredients can be elevated to create something truly unforgettable. This dish is not only delicious but also packed with protein, making it an excellent vegetarian option that leaves you feeling satisfied and nourished. The balance of heat, saltiness, and a hint of sweetness is what makes Dubu Jorim Spicy Braised Tofu a perennial favorite.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting authentic Dubu Jorim Spicy Braised Tofu requires a few key ingredients, most of which are readily available in Asian markets or even well-stocked supermarkets.

For the Tofu:
*   1 block (14-16 oz) firm or extra-firm tofu
*   2-3 tablespoons cooking oil (e.g., vegetable, canola, or grapeseed oil)

For the Sauce:
*   3-4 tablespoons soy sauce (low sodium preferred)
*   2-3 tablespoons gochugaru (Korean chili powder) – adjust to your spice preference
*   1 tablespoon gochujang (Korean chili paste) – optional, for deeper color and flavor
*   1 tablespoon sugar or rice syrup (or other sweetener like maple syrup)
*   1 tablespoon minced garlic (about 3-4 cloves)
*   1 teaspoon sesame oil
*   1/2 teaspoon black pepper
*   1/2 cup water or vegetable broth

For Garnish and Aromatics:
*   2-3 green onions, chopped (reserve some for garnish)
*   1 small onion, thinly sliced (optional, adds sweetness)
*   1-2 fresh red or green chilies, sliced (optional, for extra heat and color)
*   1 teaspoon sesame seeds (for garnish)

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to create your own delicious Dubu Jorim Spicy Braised Tofu:

1.  **Prepare the Tofu:** Remove the tofu from its packaging and drain any excess water. Wrap the block in a few layers of paper towels or a clean kitchen towel. Place a heavy object (like a cutting board with a few cans on top) on the tofu for at least 30 minutes to an hour to press out as much water as possible. This step is crucial for firming up the tofu and allowing it to absorb the sauce better.
2.  **Slice and Pan-Fry Tofu:** Once pressed, slice the tofu into 1/2-inch thick rectangles or squares. Heat the cooking oil in a large non-stick pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Carefully place the tofu slices in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Fry for 3-5 minutes per side, or until golden brown and slightly crispy. Remove the fried tofu from the pan and set aside on a plate lined with paper towels to absorb any excess oil.
3.  **Prepare the Sauce:** While the tofu is frying or resting, combine all the sauce ingredients (soy sauce, gochugaru, gochujang, sugar/rice syrup, minced garlic, sesame oil, black pepper, and water/vegetable broth) in a small bowl. Whisk well until thoroughly combined and the sugar has dissolved.
4.  **Sauté Aromatics (Optional):** If using, add the sliced onion to the same pan (add a little more oil if needed) and sauté for 2-3 minutes until softened and translucent. Add half of the chopped green onions and fresh chilies (if using) and sauté for another minute until fragrant.
5.  **Braise the Tofu:** Gently return the fried tofu slices to the pan, arranging them in a single layer over the aromatics. Pour the prepared sauce evenly over the tofu.
6.  **Simmer:** Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pan, and let it braise for 10-15 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened and been largely absorbed by the tofu. Occasionally, gently spoon the sauce over the tofu to ensure even coating.
7.  **Finish and Serve:** Remove the pan from the heat. Garnish with the remaining chopped green onions and sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving the perfect Dubu Jorim Spicy Braised Tofu is easy with a few expert tricks:

*   **Press Your Tofu Thoroughly:** This cannot be stressed enough. The drier the tofu, the better it will brown and the more sauce it will absorb, leading to a firmer texture and richer flavor. Don't skip this step!
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Pan:** When pan-frying the tofu, give each piece space. Frying in batches ensures proper browning and prevents the tofu from steaming instead of crisping.
*   **Adjust Spice to Your Liking:** The amount of gochugaru and gochujang can be tailored. For milder Dubu Jorim, reduce the gochugaru to 1-2 tablespoons and omit the gochujang. For extra heat, add more chili powder or a pinch of fresh bird's eye chilies.
*   **Taste and Adjust Sauce:** Before braising, taste a tiny bit of the sauce. Adjust sweetness, saltiness, or spice as needed. A perfectly balanced sauce is key to a delicious dish.
*   **Let it Rest (Optional):** Like many braised dishes, Dubu Jorim can sometimes taste even better the next day as the flavors meld and deepen. It's excellent served warm or at room temperature.

## Serving Suggestions

Dubu Jorim Spicy Braised Tofu is incredibly versatile and pairs wonderfully with a variety of dishes. Traditionally, it's served as a banchan (side dish) alongside a bowl of freshly steamed white rice. The rice is perfect for soaking up every drop of the delectable spicy sauce.

You can also enjoy it as a main course, especially when paired with other Korean vegetarian side dishes like seasoned spinach (sigeumchi namul), bean sprout salad (kongnamul muchim), or kimchi. For a more substantial meal, consider serving it with a simple clear vegetable soup. The vibrant colors and bold flavors of Dubu Jorim make it a fantastic centerpiece for any Korean-inspired meal, offering a satisfying and wholesome option that caters to vegetarian preferences.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Dubu Jorim Spicy Braised Tofu recipe is fantastic, don't hesitate to experiment with variations to suit your taste or what you have on hand:

*   **Add Vegetables:** Enhance the nutritional value and texture by adding quick-cooking vegetables during the braising step. Sliced mushrooms (shiitake or button), zucchini, bell peppers, or even thin carrot strips work beautifully. Add them a few minutes before the tofu is fully braised so they cook through but retain a slight bite.
*   **Different Tofu Types:** While firm or extra-firm tofu is recommended for its texture, you can use medium-firm tofu if you prefer a softer consistency, just be extra gentle when handling it. Silken tofu is generally too delicate for this preparation.
*   **Sweetener Alternatives:** If you don't have sugar or rice syrup, honey, agave nectar, or even a tiny splash of mirin (sweet rice wine) can be used to add a touch of sweetness.
*   **Make it Less Spicy:** For those sensitive to heat, significantly reduce the gochugaru and omit the gochujang. You can add a bit more soy sauce or a touch of miso paste for depth of flavor without the spice.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** A tiny pinch of smoked paprika can add a subtle smoky depth, complementing the savory notes of the dish.
*   **Nutty Boost:** A spoonful of finely crushed toasted peanuts or cashews sprinkled on top just before serving can add a delightful crunch and nutty flavor.

Dubu Jorim Spicy Braised Tofu is more than just a dish; it's an experience of robust flavors, comforting warmth, and the simple joy of plant-based cooking. Whether you're a seasoned Korean food enthusiast or new to its wonders, this spicy braised tofu is a delightful and healthy addition to any meal rotation. Give it a try, and prepare to be captivated by its irresistible charm!
